test_layer: Exact production CRC, payload, fragment and planner functions plus current production WorkBudget. Scheduler ticks, connection state and GATT acceptance are simulated. The real TX task descriptor checkpoint is represented explicitly; full task release paths are reviewed in source, not claimed as hardware execution.

scenarios.case: 600-byte payload, MTU247, 3 fragments, constant SDK tick
2304-byte payload, MTU247, 11 fragments, constant SDK tick
SDK consumes one tick per fragment

scenarios.result: Next fragment is rejected in each case even within a batch; no completed message or premature slot release.

scenarios.case: GATT fails at fragment5, after one full batch
scenarios.result: First send error returned, message dropped, slot retained until caller returns.

review_findings: Every fragment still calls the original connection validation before touching the GATT boundary.
At most four successful fast fragments run before a scheduling checkpoint while more fragments remain. One elapsed tick triggers a checkpoint sooner; unsigned subtraction handles tick wrap.
The final fragment returns to the unchanged descriptor loop checkpoint. No complete message or fast-failure path can permanently bypass the global budget.
The payload slot and shared fragment scratch remain owned by the same TX worker; no new allocator, release, task or concurrent sender was introduced.
This is a local scheduling unit change. Neither notification acceptance, fragmentSent, zero fragmentError nor connected state establishes PC receipt or unlimited radio capacity.
Existing SDK call execution time is not bounded by this gate; it can only act between returns. No watchdog is fed or disabled.

model_correction.description: Initial test expected idle-unknown blocking immediately at Init, before two ticks elapsed. The independent model was corrected to advance two ticks after Init. The failed assertion was in the model, not a production defect.

verdict: No new confirmed P0/P1 in the reviewed batching increment. Target build and HIL throughput/idle-progress verification remain root-owned.
